requirements.evidence: Migrations match the schema incl. `owner_seq` storedAs + unique `entity_memberships_one_owner` (create_entity_memberships_table.php:26-27) and `entities_slug_unique` (create_entities_table.php:17). Policies implement every ability (EntityPolicy.php, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:35-48). `pick` 403s before touching the session and logs on `audit` (EntityController.php:16-25). Members: duplicate -> error on `email` (Members.php:43), `in:admin,employee` (Members.php:62), owner/last-manager guard (Members.php:82-92). Settings: `#[Locked] public Entity $entity`, slug unique ignoring self (Settings.php:44), transfer checks admin-of-this-entity, not caller, owner vanished -> 403, demote-then-promote in a transaction (Settings.php:78-93). Dashboard settings link and owner notice behind `@can('manageSettings')`. Routes and lang keys present in both locales. Gaps: no tests at all, so nothing proves the contract; role is shown as the raw enum value `$membership->role->value` (members.blade.php:14) rather than translated text; delete() is not wrapped in a transaction (Settings.php:60-61).

conventions.evidence: Conventions require test-first and 'No production code without a test', but the diff adds no test file. Domain writes are supposed to go through `app/Actions/*`, yet addMember/assignRole/removeMember/save/delete/transfer all write directly from the components (Members.php:48, 70, 91; Settings.php:46, 60-61, 89-90). Settings `$name`, `$slug` and `$targetMembershipId` have no `#[Validate]` and are validated with inline arrays instead (Settings.php:21-25, 41-44), and assignRole uses `Validator::make` (Members.php:60-62) where the project pattern is `#[Validate]`. `pick` does its own membership check (`abort(403)`, EntityController.php:16-18) instead of going through the policy. Views use bare `<input>`/`<button>` with no Bulma form classes or Blade components. On the plus side, CHANGELOG and docs/database-schema.md are updated, `$fillable` is set, and the policies are registered.

security.evidence: Every Livewire action authorizes on the server: Members `authorize('update')`/`authorize('assignRole')`/`authorize('delete')` (Members.php:34, 66, 81) and Settings re-fetches the entity and checks `authorize('manageSettings')` (Settings.php:39, 56, 74). Client IDs are resolved within the bound entity: `$this->entity->memberships()->findOrFail($membershipId)` (Members.php:64, 79), and transfer uses `$entity->memberships()->whereKey(...)` (Settings.php:78). The entity is `#[Locked]`, all output uses `{{ }}`, and `$fillable` is set. Minor gaps: `targetMembershipId`/`name`/`slug` are not declared validated properties, and a concurrent duplicate add would surface as a unique-constraint 500 instead of a validation error.

tests.evidence: The diff adds no Pest/PHPUnit test file. There is nothing for the migrations, the DB one-owner constraint, the policies, `entity.pick`, the three Livewire components, the unauthorized-call and tamper cases the Livewire policy requires, or the localized texts. Only factories were added (EntityFactory.php, EntityMembershipFactory.php).

simplicity.evidence: Code is direct and reuses Eloquent relations and scopes (`Entity::owner()` = `hasOne(...)->owner()`). Small duplications: the owner/admin membership check is repeated in EntityPolicy::update, ::delete and EntityMembershipPolicy::assignRole/delete; Members.php:62 hard-codes `in:admin,employee` instead of using `UserRole::manageable()`, which is defined and unused; the owner checks at Members.php:68-70 and 83-85 repeat what the policy and DB already guarantee.

readability.evidence: Methods are short with clear names and PHPDoc on the relations. Nits: the `User::entities()` PHPDoc says `BelongsToMany<User, $this>` but should be `<Entity, ...>` (User.php:44); the `@param mixed $membershipId` params are untyped; the dashboard's secondary nav reuses the `ui.main_navigation` aria-label (dashboard.blade.php:10).

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: models, migrations, factories, policies, the pick controller, three Livewire pages, routes, lang keys, and the schema doc/CHANGELOG updates. No onboarding, switcher, middleware or navbar work was added.

issues.explanation: No tests ship with the change, so the project's mandatory TDD rule and the Livewire definition of done (happy path, validation failure, unauthorized call and tamper test per action) are not met.
Domain writes (add/assign/remove member, update/delete entity, transfer ownership) are done directly in Livewire components instead of `app/Actions/*` use-case classes.
Settings properties lack `#[Validate]`, and assignRole uses `Validator::make` instead of the project's `#[Validate]` + `$this->validate()` pattern.
The pick endpoint authorizes with an ad-hoc membership check and `abort(403)` rather than through `EntityPolicy::view`.
Deleting memberships and soft-deleting the entity are not wrapped in a transaction, so a failure between the two can leave an entity with no members.
The role is shown as the raw enum value (`owner`/`admin`/`employee`) rather than as text from `lang/*/ui.php`.
Forms use bare inputs and buttons with no Bulma `field`/`input`/`button` classes or Blade components, unlike the project's UI conventions.
Hard-codes `in:admin,employee` instead of deriving the rule from `UserRole::manageable()`, which is defined but unused.
The PHPDoc generic for `entities()` says `BelongsToMany<User, $this>` but the related model is `Entity`.
The page-level nav reuses the `ui.main_navigation` aria-label, which may clash with the layout's main navbar landmark.

review.summary: The change implements the entities data model (including the DB-enforced single owner), both policies, the pick endpoint and the dashboard/members/settings Livewire pages, with solid server-side authorization, entity-scoped lookups and a correct atomic ownership transfer. It ships no tests at all, which breaks the project's mandatory TDD and Livewire definition of done. It also bypasses the `app/Actions` pattern and `#[Validate]` conventions, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
